title: Pornography, Family Vulnerability, and Hifz al-Nasl : A Maqasid al-Shari’ah Synthesis
text_snippet: Pornography, Family Vulnerability, and Hifz al-Nasl : A Maqasid al-Shari’ah Synthesis Digital access to pornography has intensified concerns about adolescent sexual behavior, aggression, caregiving, and broader family vulnerability. This study examines how these empirically documented vulnerabilities may be interpreted through hifz al-nasl within the framework of maqasid al-shari'ah. Using a qualitative conceptual literature synthesis, seven purposively selected empirical sources on pornography exposure and problematic use, sexual behavior and violence, postpartum bonding following sexual violence, and intergenerational neglect and victimization were analyzed alongside classical and contemporary maqasid scholarship. The synthesis identifies three empirical domains: pornography-related behavioral and sexual vulnerabilities, reproductive and caregiving adversity associated with sexual violence, and intergenerational neglect and victimization. The evidence does not establish a linear causal pathway from pornography exposure to family dysfunction, and findings concerning pornography and aggression remain heterogeneous. title: Interactive Video Media and Students’ IPAS Learning Outcomes: A One-Group Pretest–Posttest Study
text_snippet: Interactive Video Media and Students’ IPAS Learning Outcomes: A One-Group Pretest–Posttest Study Interactive video can support the presentation of visually rich learning content by integrating audiovisual information with opportunities for learner interaction. This study examined differences in students’ IPAS learning outcomes before and after the use of interactive video media among fourth-grade students at SD Negeri 57 Banda Aceh. A quantitative pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with 27 students. Students’ cognitive learning outcomes were measured using a 22-item multiple-choice test that had undergone item validity and reliability testing, with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of .744. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize pretest and posttest performance, while differences between the paired scores were analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test because the posttest scores did not meet the stated normality criterion. The mean score increased from 49.556 on the pretest to 86.741 on the posttest. All 27 participants obtained higher posttest scores, with no negative ranks or ties. title: Child Protection Institutions and Religious Communities in Preventing and Responding to Child Sexual Violence in Deli Serdang
text_snippet: Child Protection Institutions and Religious Communities in Preventing and Responding to Child Sexual Violence in Deli Serdang Child sexual violence requires responses that combine victim protection with prevention within families and communities. This study examines the responsive and preventive roles of the Child Protection Agency (Lembaga Perlindungan Anak, LPA) of Deli Serdang, the preventive perspectives and practices articulated by Islamic and Buddhist community representatives, and the relationship between these institutional and community-based domains. A qualitative descriptive case-study design was employed using semi-structured interviews with four purposively selected institutional informants and documentary data, including anonymized records of five child sexual violence cases and LPA assistance-monitoring records from June 2026. The findings show that LPA performs responsive functions through safety assurance, risk assessment, medical and psychological assistance, legal accompaniment, and confidentiality protection, alongside preventive body safety education for children and parents. Islamic and Buddhist representatives articulate a different preventive domain centered on family guidance, moral education, parental responsibility, interpersonal boundaries, compassion, and self-discipline. title: Uqubat Ta’zir for Child Offenders Convicted of Rape Under Aceh’s Jinayat Law: Balancing Child Protection and Victim Justice
text_snippet: Uqubat Ta’zir for Child Offenders Convicted of Rape Under Aceh’s Jinayat Law: Balancing Child Protection and Victim Justice The imposition of uqubat ta’zir (a discretionary punishment under Aceh’s Islamic criminal law) on a child offender convicted of rape requires courts to reconcile child-specific protection and rehabilitation with recognition of the harm experienced by a child victim. This article examines Banda Aceh Sharia Court Decision No. 1/JN.Anak/2023/MS.Bna. It asks what legal and nonlegal considerations supported the punishment and to what extent the court’s reasoning balanced protection of the child offenders with justice for the child victim. The study employed doctrinal legal research using statutory and case approaches. Its primary materials included the decision, Aceh Qanun No. 6 of 2014—a regional regulation governing jinayat (Islamic criminal law) in Aceh—and Indonesia’s juvenile justice, child-protection, and victim-recovery legislation. The court imposed 24 months of pembinaan (structured guidance and development) in a Juvenile Special Development Institution (Lembaga Pembinaan Khusus Anak, LPKA), compared with the prosecutor’s request for 48 months. title: Self-Reward Among Final-Year Female Students in An Islamic Religious Education Program: Meanings and Boundaries of Gratitude, Excess, and Waste
text_snippet: Self-Reward Among Final-Year Female Students in An Islamic Religious Education Program: Meanings and Boundaries of Gratitude, Excess, and Waste This study examined how female students in the final year of the Islamic Religious Education (Pendidikan Agama Islam, PAI) program at Universitas Islam Nahdlatul Ulama Jepara understood self-reward and constructed boundaries among shukr (gratitude), isrāf (excess), and tabdhīr (wasteful expenditure). The study employed a qualitative approach with a phenomenological orientation. Preliminary screening involved 16 female students in their final year and examined variation in self-reward frequency, form, expenditure, motives, and ethical considerations. Five participants representing contrasting practices were then purposively selected through maximum-variation sampling. Data were collected between March and May 2026 through semi-structured, in-depth interviews supported by contextual nonparticipant observation and were analyzed manually using an interactive qualitative model. Participants understood self-reward as an expression of gratitude, recognition of effort or achievement, personal celebration, and emotional recovery. title: Legal Protection of Hajj and Umrah Pilgrims Under Indonesia’s Amended Pilgrimage Law: A Doctrinal Analysis
text_snippet: Legal Protection of Hajj and Umrah Pilgrims Under Indonesia’s Amended Pilgrimage Law: A Doctrinal Analysis Hajj and Umrah services in Indonesia combine religious observance with public administration, cross-border mobility, financial transactions, and commercial service relationships, exposing pilgrims to both regulatory and contractual risks. Law No. 14 of 2025 amended Indonesia’s sector-specific pilgrimage legislation, but the relationship among pilgrims’ statutory rights, governmental responsibility, organizer accountability, and general consumer protection requires systematic clarification. This article examines how the amended framework regulates pilgrims’ rights and protection, allocates responsibilities between the government and pilgrimage organizers, and structures supervision, accountability, and legal remedies. The study employs doctrinal legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches. Its primary legal materials comprise Law No. 8 of 2019 as amended by Law No. 14 of 2025, Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection, and relevant implementing regulations. These materials are analyzed through grammatical, systematic, and doctrinal interpretation. The findings demonstrate that Indonesian law does not establish a uniform protection model. title: Involvement in Higgs Domino Island and Its Perceived Behavioral Implications in Gampong Lamdingin, Banda Aceh
text_snippet: Involvement in Higgs Domino Island and Its Perceived Behavioral Implications in Gampong Lamdingin, Banda Aceh Digital games that incorporate betting mechanisms and allow virtual chips to be exchanged for money may develop from recreational activities into forms of online gambling. This study examines the factors associated with residents’ involvement in Higgs Domino Island and the perceived implications of such involvement for religious routines, social relations, education, productivity, and economic management in Gampong Lamdingin, Banda Aceh. The study employed a descriptive qualitative case-study design. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observation, and documentation involving 13 purposively selected informants consisting of players and individuals who interacted closely with them. The data were analyzed through repeated familiarization, coding, thematic grouping, comparison across accounts, and interpretive synthesis. Credibility was strengthened by comparing information across informants and data-collection techniques. The findings indicate three recurring pathways of involvement: peer and environmental exposure, repeated play that became increasingly difficult to control, and expectations of rapid economic gain. title: Negotiating the Continuity of Blangikhan: An AGIL Analysis of Institutional, Customary, Religious, and Community Roles in Negeri Olok Gading
text_snippet: Negotiating the Continuity of Blangikhan: An AGIL Analysis of Institutional, Customary, Religious, and Community Roles in Negeri Olok Gading The continuity of local religious traditions depends on relationships among community authorities, public institutions, and residents, yet previous studies have often examined these actors separately. This study analyzes how social functions are distributed among the actors involved in Blangikhan, a pre-Ramadan purification tradition in Negeri Olok Gading, Bandar Lampung, and how they negotiate public promotion, religious interpretation, youth participation, and value transmission. A qualitative approach with a sociological orientation was employed. Data were collected in 2026 through nonparticipant observation, document review, and in-depth interviews with six purposively selected informants: one Tourism Office representative, one customary leader, one religious leader, and three community members. The data were coded using Parsons’s AGIL framework and compared through source triangulation. The findings indicate that the Tourism Office primarily supported adaptation through facilitation and promotion, religious leadership contributed to the formulation of legitimate purposes, community participation supported integration, and customary leadership maintained inherited patterns. title: Religion and Local Cultural Identity in Indonesia’s Plural Society: A Sociological Thematic Synthesis
text_snippet: Religion and Local Cultural Identity in Indonesia’s Plural Society: A Sociological Thematic Synthesis Religion is deeply involved in the construction and transmission of local cultural identity in Indonesia. However, its relationship with local culture is neither uniformly integrative nor inherently conflictual. Previous studies have documented particular communities, traditions, and religious encounters, but the mechanisms through which religion contributes to cultural continuity, social integration, and contestation remain insufficiently synthesized. This article examines how religion participates in the formation, maintenance, and transformation of local cultural identity in Indonesia’s plural society. It uses a qualitative structured thematic review of scholarly publications located through Google Scholar, Garuda, and Crossref using Indonesian and English search terms. The review primarily covers publications from 2016 to 2025 while retaining earlier works required for conceptual and historical interpretation. The sources were analyzed across four domains: normative values, ritual and symbolic practices, institutional mediation, and cultural adaptation or contestation. title: Evaluating Dropshipping Through Hadith and Islamic Commercial Law: Unauthorized Sales, Salam, and Wakalah bi Al-Ujrah
text_snippet: Evaluating Dropshipping Through Hadith and Islamic Commercial Law: Unauthorized Sales, Salam, and Wakalah bi Al-Ujrah The expansion of dropshipping has renewed questions in Islamic commercial jurisprudence concerning ownership, authorization, possession, delivery risk, and contractual uncertainty. Although previous studies have examined dropshipping through Islamic jurisprudence and hadith, they have not consistently integrated hadith source mapping and selected transmission issues with a comparative assessment of different contractual models. This article examines three normative configurations: dropshipping conducted without supplier authorization, dropshipping structured as salam, and dropshipping conducted through wakālah bi al-ujrah. It employs focused qualitative library research using major hadith collections, transmitter biographies, classical commentaries, and relevant contemporary studies. The analysis combines takhrīj al-ḥadīth with a focused review of selected transmission issues, textual context, classical commentary, and fiqh al-ḥadīth. title: Integrating Good Waqf Governance and Visionary Leadership in Pesantren Waqf Management: Institutional Law as an Enabling Prerequisite
text_snippet: Integrating Good Waqf Governance and Visionary Leadership in Pesantren Waqf Management: Institutional Law as an Enabling Prerequisite Waqf management in Indonesian pesantren faces persistent challenges related to institutional status, administrative capacity, accountability, leadership, and productive asset development. Existing studies generally examine Good Waqf Governance (GWG), leadership in Islamic educational institutions, and institutional law as separate domains, leaving their interaction insufficiently integrated in the context of pesantren-based waqf management. This study develops the Integrated Pesantren Waqf Governance Model (IPTGM) as a preliminary conceptual framework combining institutional law, GWG, and visionary leadership. A Systematic Literature Review guided by PRISMA 2020 was conducted using publications identified through Google Scholar, SINTA, Scopus, and supplementary reference searching. Of 124 initially identified records, 21 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2025 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the synthesis. The review was complemented by a focused normative analysis of Law No. 41 of 2004 on Waqf and Law No. 18 of 2019 on Pesantren. title: Evaluating A School–Home Screen-Time Policy: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study at TK Islam Alam Nusantara, Indonesia
text_snippet: Evaluating A School–Home Screen-Time Policy: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study at TK Islam Alam Nusantara, Indonesia Young children’s screen use occurs primarily within the home, limiting the ability of schools to align family media routines with classroom learning demands. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of an initial school-developed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for screen-time management at TK Islam Alam Nusantara in Bandung, Indonesia. The study employed an embedded mixed-methods design in which qualitative policy evaluation constituted the primary component, supported by a 30-day single-group pretest–posttest assessment. Five children with relatively high screen exposure and marked classroom attention or behavioral difficulties were selected through purposive extreme-case sampling. Data were collected through parent and teacher questionnaires, post-simulation interviews, structured classroom observations, and textual analysis of the initial SOP. The findings identified three operational weaknesses in the initial policy: ambiguous instructions, limited practical support for families, and the absence of a follow-up consultation mechanism. title: Women’s Agency and Relational Support in Resisting Patriarchy: A Structural Analysis of When Life Gives You Tangerines
text_snippet: Women’s Agency and Relational Support in Resisting Patriarchy: A Structural Analysis of When Life Gives You Tangerines Patriarchal resistance in popular media is often interpreted primarily as an individual struggle by female characters, leaving the role of interpersonal support within family relationships insufficiently examined. This study analyzes how resistance to patriarchy is represented through Oh Ae-Sun’s actions across her life course and how Yang Gwan-Sik’s support contributes to negotiating patriarchal expectations within the family in the Korean drama When Life Gives You Tangerines. The study employed a descriptive qualitative design using deductive qualitative content analysis of all 16 episodes. The data consisted of scenes, dialogue, actions, nonverbal expressions, and family interactions, which were analyzed through three structures adapted from Sylvia Walby’s theory: household production, culture institutions, and sexuality. The findings show that Ae-Sun’s individual resistance is most explicit in her persistence in maintaining her literary identity, challenging gendered exclusion from leadership, and supporting educational opportunities for her daughter. title: Women’s Religious Journeys and Muslim Identity Reconstruction: A Phenomenological Study of Converts in Medan, Indonesia
text_snippet: Women’s Religious Journeys and Muslim Identity Reconstruction: A Phenomenological Study of Converts in Medan, Indonesia Religious conversion is not completed through the formal adoption of a new religious affiliation but develops through religious learning, social negotiation, and identity reconstruction. This study examines how women affiliated with Mualaf Center Kampung Madras in Medan interpret their religious journeys and how social interactions contribute to the formation of their identities as Muslim women. The study employed a qualitative phenomenological design involving five women converts aged 31–60 as primary participants and the head of Mualaf Center Kampung Madras as a supporting key informant. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, nonparticipant observation, and documentation. The data were analyzed through bracketing, intuiting, analyzing, and describing, while symbolic interactionism was used to interpret the construction of religious meaning and identity. The findings identified four interrelated themes: diverse pathways to conversion, post-conversion challenges and religious adjustment, social support and the role of the Mualaf Center, and the reconstruction of the self as a Muslim woman. title: Unlogic Birth Education, Perceived Husband Assertiveness, and Mode of Delivery: A Retrospective Observational Study
text_snippet: Unlogic Birth Education, Perceived Husband Assertiveness, and Mode of Delivery: A Retrospective Observational Study The increasing rate of caesarean section has raised concerns about childbirth interventions performed without clear medical indications. Antenatal education may support childbirth preparation and informed decision-making, although the mechanisms linking such education to mode of delivery remain uncertain. This study examined the association between participation in the Unlogic Birth (UB) educational program and mode of delivery and assessed whether perceived husband assertiveness mediated this association. A retrospective observational study was conducted among 72 postpartum women who had received antenatal care at Klinik Utama Cikal Mulia, Jakarta, Indonesia. Participants were selected using purposive sampling and classified according to their participation in UB education. Perceived husband assertiveness was measured using a 12-item questionnaire completed by wives, while mode of delivery was verified through clinical records. Direct and indirect associations among the variables were examined using an exploratory structural-path analysis. Of the 72 participants, 58 had participated in UB education and 14 had not. title: Nonformal Cultural Education, the Preservation of Benjang, and Cultural Awareness: A Case Study of Sekolah Benjang Indonesia
text_snippet: Nonformal Cultural Education, the Preservation of Benjang, and Cultural Awareness: A Case Study of Sekolah Benjang Indonesia This study examines the nonformal education strategies implemented at Sekolah Benjang Indonesia (Indonesian Benjang School) to preserve Benjang, a traditional art form associated with Ujung Berung, Bandung City, and to explore their contribution to cultural awareness among participants. The study employed a qualitative case study design. Data were collected from seven informants, comprising the founder of the Wallagri Foundation, the school principal, a Benjang trainer, two students, and two community members. Data collection involved in-depth interviews, direct observation, document analysis, and visual documentation of training sessions, public performances, cultural outreach activities, and the school’s launching event. The data were analyzed through reduction, display, and conclusion drawing or verification, supported by source triangulation, technique triangulation, and member checking. title: Mental Health Experiences of Female Adolescent Santri Following Islamic Coaching with the I.S.L.A.M Model: A Qualitative Study in an Indonesian Pesantren
text_snippet: Mental Health Experiences of Female Adolescent Santri Following Islamic Coaching with the I.S.L.A.M Model: A Qualitative Study in an Indonesian Pesantren This study examines the perceived mental health experiences of female adolescent santri after participating in Islamic Coaching with the I.S.L.A.M Model in an Indonesian pesantren. Adolescent mental health remains a serious concern in Indonesia, including among santri who live within structured religious, academic, and residential environments. Although coaching has been used as a non-clinical form of support, limited qualitative research has examined how spiritually grounded coaching is experienced by adolescent santri in Islamic boarding school settings. This study used an exploratory qualitative design with a phenomenological orientation. Five female santri aged 14 to 17 years who had completed Islamic Coaching sessions using the I.S.L.A.M Model were selected through purposive sampling, and one additional informant was included to provide contextual information. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings show that participants perceived the coaching process as a relatively safe and structured space for emotional expression, self-reflection, social boundary-setting, and spiritual coping. title: When Financial Aid Is Not Enough: The Smart Indonesia Program, Social Capital, and Learning Quality at MAN 1 Pidie
text_snippet: When Financial Aid Is Not Enough: The Smart Indonesia Program, Social Capital, and Learning Quality at MAN 1 Pidie The Smart Indonesia Program (Program Indonesia Pintar, PIP) is designed to reduce educational costs for students from poor and vulnerable households. Its role in widening access is widely recognised, yet its contribution to learning quality remains less direct. This article examines how PIP shaped educational access and learning quality at Madrasah Aliyah Negeri 1 Pidie, Aceh, Indonesia, with particular attention to the role of social capital. Using a qualitative case study design, data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews with beneficiary students, parents, teachers, and the madrasah principal, and documentation related to programme implementation. The analysis draws on Bourdieu’s concept of social capital to explain why financial assistance does not always produce equal educational outcomes. PIP reduced routine schooling costs, including uniforms, books, stationery, and transportation, and helped students from low-income families remain enrolled. It also increased confidence and supported school participation among several beneficiaries. However, its influence on learning quality was less consistent. title: Negotiating Self-Expression, Digital Privacy, and Religious Identity on Instagram’s Close Friends: A Qualitative Study of Mosque Youth
text_snippet: Negotiating Self-Expression, Digital Privacy, and Religious Identity on Instagram’s Close Friends: A Qualitative Study of Mosque Youth This study examines how mosque youth use Instagram’s Close Friends feature to negotiate self-expression, digital privacy, and religious identity. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed with eight members of the Nurul Hidayah Mosque Youth Organization in Pertahanan Village, aged 17–20 years. Participants were selected purposively because they were active Instagram users who used Close Friends to share personal content. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews conducted in April 2026, one month of non-participant digital observation of relevant Close Friends stories, and consented documentation. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, supported by source and method triangulation and member checking. Close Friends functioned as a semi-private communication space in which participants shared personal opinions, relationship-related experiences, academic pressures, emotional conditions, religious reflections, social criticism, and everyday activities with selected audiences. title: Gender Equality Policy Communication in Formal Workplaces: An Exploratory Study of Women Workers’ Experiences
text_snippet: Gender Equality Policy Communication in Formal Workplaces: An Exploratory Study of Women Workers’ Experiences Gender equality policies in formal workplaces do not automatically produce substantive equality in everyday organisational practice. Their implementation is shaped not only by the existence of formal rules, but also by how such policies are communicated, interpreted, and connected to employees’ workplace experiences. This study examines how women workers experience and interpret the communication of gender equality policies in formal workplace settings. Using a qualitative descriptive-exploratory design, data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with four women workers from different organisational contexts: industry, government or policy consultancy, banking or finance, and digital technology. The data were analysed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, with attention to dialogic space, employee participation, policy legitimacy, and the internalisation of gender equality values. The findings identify four patterns of policy communication: formal communication, deliberative-participatory communication, compliance-based communication, and digital-participatory communication. title: Fasād fī al-Arḍ and Illegal Gold Mining in Jambur Tarutung: An Ecological Reading of Tafsir al-Munir
text_snippet: Fasād fī al-Arḍ and Illegal Gold Mining in Jambur Tarutung: An Ecological Reading of Tafsir al-Munir Illegal gold mining, known in Indonesia as Pertambangan Emas Tanpa Izin (PETI), has generated serious ecological and social consequences in rural communities. Although Islamic environmental ethics and ecological tafsir have received growing scholarly attention, many studies remain normative and have not sufficiently connected Qur’anic exegesis with empirical ecological realities. This article examines ecological degradation caused by PETI in Lingkungan III Jambur Tarutung, Pasar Kotanopan Village, Mandailing Natal Regency, North Sumatra, through the concept of fasād fī al-arḍ in Tafsir al-Munir by Wahbah az-Zuhaili. The study employed a qualitative case study design combined with thematic Qur’anic interpretation (tafsīr maudhu‘i). Primary data were collected through field observations and semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected informants, consisting of community leaders, religious leaders, and community members connected to mining-related activities. Secondary data were obtained from Tafsir al-Munir, ecological tafsir literature, maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah studies, and previous research on illegal mining and environmental degradation. title: From Qur’anic Normative Understanding to Institutional Practice: Zakat, Infaq, and Sadaqah Management at Baznas Batu Bara Regency
text_snippet: From Qur’anic Normative Understanding to Institutional Practice: Zakat, Infaq, and Sadaqah Management at Baznas Batu Bara Regency This study examines how Qur’anic verses on zakat, infaq, and sadaqah are understood and operationalized in the institutional practices of BAZNAS Batu Bara Regency, Indonesia. While previous studies have largely discussed zakat effectiveness, productive zakat, zakat literacy, and the impact of Islamic philanthropy on mustahik welfare, limited attention has been given to how regional zakat institutions translate Qur’anic normative understanding into program governance. This study employed a qualitative case study design. Data were collected through interviews with BAZNAS administrators, a community figure, and mustahik beneficiaries, supported by limited observation and institutional documentation. title: Jakartan Slang as a Generational Identity Marker and the Reduced Use of Javanese in Peer Interaction among Generation Z Students at Universitas Negeri Semarang
text_snippet: Jakartan Slang as a Generational Identity Marker and the Reduced Use of Javanese in Peer Interaction among Generation Z Students at Universitas Negeri Semarang The increasing use of Jakartan slang among Generation Z has become a visible feature of youth communication in Indonesian university settings. While previous studies have examined the forms, meanings, and social functions of slang, less attention has been given to how slang shapes generational identity and affects the use of local languages in campus peer interaction. This study examines Jakartan slang as a generational identity marker among Generation Z students at the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences, Universitas Negeri Semarang, and explores its implications for the reduced use of Javanese in selected peer interactions. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the study draws on semi-structured interviews with 10 students, qualitative questionnaire responses from 10 Javanese-speaking students, and unstructured observation in campus-related settings. The data were analyzed thematically and interpreted through Social Identity Theory, particularly the concepts of social categorization, social identification, and social comparison. title: From Read-Aloud Practice to Interactive Storytelling: Teachers’ Strategies for Using Storybooks in Early Childhood Learning at Tadika Alfikh Orchadch
text_snippet: From Read-Aloud Practice to Interactive Storytelling: Teachers’ Strategies for Using Storybooks in Early Childhood Learning at Tadika Alfikh Orchadch Storybooks are widely used in early childhood education to support language stimulation, children’s engagement, and the introduction of simple moral values. However, classroom practice often remains limited to one-way read-aloud activities, leaving children with few opportunities to respond, interpret, and participate actively in storytelling. This study examines teachers’ strategies for using storybooks interactively with young children at Tadika Alfikh Orchadch, identifies the obstacles teachers face, and describes the efforts made by teachers and the institution to improve storytelling activities. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through classroom observations, teacher interviews, and learning documentation involving six teachers and one class of ten children aged four to five years. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, while trustworthiness was strengthened through technique triangulation. title: Custom, Economic Roles, and Islamic Values in Shaping The Communication Patterns of Coastal Women in Bengkulu City, Indonesia
text_snippet: Custom, Economic Roles, and Islamic Values in Shaping The Communication Patterns of Coastal Women in Bengkulu City, Indonesia This study examines how custom, economic roles, and Islamic values shape the communication patterns of coastal women in Bengkulu City, Indonesia. It argues that women’s communication in coastal communities should be understood as a socially constructed and domain-specific practice rather than merely as a gendered speaking style. Using a qualitative approach with a focused ethnography design, the study was conducted in three coastal sub-districts: Malabero, Berkas, and Sumber Jaya. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews, participant observation, and document study involving 24 women, including fish traders, fishermen’s wives, seafood processors, and members of women’s fisher groups. The data were analyzed thematically. The results indicate that Melayu Bengkulu customary norms tend to shape women’s communication as careful, indirect, and oriented toward politeness in family and community forums. Economic roles in fish trading and seafood processing create more assertive communicative spaces, particularly in markets and household economic decision-making. title: Prophetic Communication in Tafsir Al-Mishbah: Tabshir–Indzar, Hiwar, and Amtsal as A Model of Transcendental Communication
text_snippet: Prophetic Communication in Tafsir Al-Mishbah: Tabshir–Indzar, Hiwar, and Amtsal as A Model of Transcendental Communication This study examines prophetic communication in the Qur’an through the interpretive framework of Tafsir Al-Mishbah by Muhammad Quraish Shihab and maps its major communicative strategies into a persuasive-dialogic model relevant to contemporary da'wah. The study employs a qualitative library research design with Tafsir Al-Mishbah as the primary source, supported by relevant scholarship in Qur’anic exegesis, Islamic communication, and contemporary religious communication. The unit of analysis consists of Quraish Shihab’s interpretive constructions of selected Qur’anic verses that reflect the communicative dimensions of prophethood. The analysis was conducted through thematic interpretation (tafsir mawḍū‘ī), close reading, thematic coding, and conceptual interpretation using persuasive, dialogic, and transcendental communication frameworks. The findings show that prophetic communication in Tafsir Al-Mishbah is structured through several interconnected strategies, namely tabshīr (encouragement and glad tidings), indzār (warning and moral caution), ḥiwār (dialogical engagement), and amtsāl (parable-based communication). title: Developing the Al-Ghazali Learning Values Scale: Initial Evidence of Validity and Reliability among Online Learners
text_snippet: Developing the Al-Ghazali Learning Values Scale: Initial Evidence of Validity and Reliability among Online Learners Learning values play an important role in shaping students’ attitudes toward knowledge, discipline, and academic responsibility. Although Al-Ghazali’s educational philosophy provides a rich framework for value-based learning, empirical instruments designed to measure these values remain limited in contemporary educational research. This study aimed to examine the initial psychometric properties of the Al-Ghazali Learning Values Scale among students engaged in online learning. The instrument was developed based on key dimensions derived from Al-Ghazali’s educational thought, including sincerity in learning, academic ethics, self-reflection, perseverance in seeking knowledge, and the integration of knowledge with moral and spiritual purposes. The preliminary scale consisted of 28 items and was administered to 263 Muslim students enrolled in online learning programs. Item validity was examined using corrected item–total correlation, while internal reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha coefficient. title: Development of Augmented Reality–Based Picture Cards for Descriptive Text Learning in Elementary School
text_snippet: Development of Augmented Reality–Based Picture Cards for Descriptive Text Learning in Elementary School This study aimed to develop and examine the feasibility of augmented reality (AR)–based picture cards for descriptive text learning in Indonesian language instruction at the elementary school level. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the Alessi and Trollip model, which consists of planning, design, and development stages. Feasibility evaluation was conducted through alpha testing involving two media experts and two material experts, as well as beta testing through a limited trial with Grade III elementary school students. Data were collected using expert validation questionnaires and student response questionnaires based on a four-point Likert scale, and analyzed descriptively by converting scores into feasibility percentages. The results of media expert validation showed feasibility scores of 66.6% (feasible) and 100% (very feasible), while material expert validation yielded scores of 95.4% (very feasible) and 75% (feasible). Student responses in the beta test reached an overall score of 90.0%, categorized as very feasible, indicating positive perceptions in terms of content clarity, visual display, language, and attractiveness. title: Ferry Irwandi’s Communication Strategies in Deconstructing Mystical Beliefs on Youtube: A Social Construction of Reality Analysis
text_snippet: Ferry Irwandi’s Communication Strategies in Deconstructing Mystical Beliefs on Youtube: A Social Construction of Reality Analysis This study aims to examine Ferry Irwandi’s communication strategies in constructing counter-narratives to mystical beliefs on Indonesian YouTube using Berger and Luckmann’s Social Construction of Reality framework. The proliferation of mystical content on YouTube has contributed to the normalization of supernatural beliefs within digital culture, particularly narratives surrounding witchcraft, indigo phenomena, and shamanistic practices. Employing a qualitative case study design, this research analyzes three YouTube videos through video observation, transcription, narrative and rhetorical analysis, and examination of audience comments. The findings indicate that Irwandi constructs externalization through critical narratives that expose logical inconsistencies in mystical claims, objectivation through empirical references and visual simplification, and internalization through audience responses marked by acceptance and resistance. Reflective content reinforces communicator credibility through clarification of positional stance, while collaborative dialogic formats strengthen rhetorical structure and expand social legitimacy for rational critique. title: Digital Control, Symbolic Power, and the Shift of Violence: Non-Physical Violence in Urban Parent–Child Relationships in Bengkulu City
text_snippet: Digital Control, Symbolic Power, and the Shift of Violence: Non-Physical Violence in Urban Parent–Child Relationships in Bengkulu City Violence against children in family settings is increasingly shifting from visible physical forms to more subtle non-physical and digitally mediated practices. Emotional neglect, verbal intimidation, and parental digital control are frequently normalized as discipline, despite their significant psychological consequences for children. This study examines the forms of non-physical and digital violence in parent–child relationships, analyzes the social factors driving this shift in violence patterns, and explores how symbolic meanings constructed through daily interactions shape differing perceptions of violence. Using a qualitative case study design grounded in the social definition paradigm and symbolic interactionism, this research was conducted in an urban residential area of Bengkulu City. Data were collected through participant observation, semi-structured interviews with 14 informants (parents and children aged 10–15), and documentation. The findings reveal that emotional, verbal, and digital violence dominate parent–child interactions, particularly through excessive monitoring, verbal threats, and unilateral restrictions on digital access. title: Audience Reception of Mental Health Representation in the Film Sleep Call: An Encoding–Decoding Analysis
text_snippet: Audience Reception of Mental Health Representation in the Film Sleep Call: An Encoding–Decoding Analysis This study examines how audiences interpret representations of mental health in the Indonesian film Sleep Call using Stuart Hall’s encoding/decoding framework. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the research draws on in-depth interviews with eight female Generation Z viewers aged 20–25 who watched the film in cinemas or via the Prime Video streaming platform. The data were analyzed through a thematic reception analysis to identify dominant-hegemonic, negotiated, and oppositional decoding positions. The findings indicate that dominant-hegemonic readings largely align with the film’s preferred meaning by framing mental health vulnerability as closely linked to economic pressure, illegal online lending, and digital loneliness. Negotiated readings accept this framing while expanding it to include relational and social dimensions, particularly the role of support systems. title: Meaning and Ethical Implications of QS. At-Ṭalaq 2–3 as the Verse of One Thousand Dinars in Hasbi Ash-Shiddieqy’s Tafsir An-Nuur
text_snippet: Meaning and Ethical Implications of QS. At-Ṭalaq 2–3 as the Verse of One Thousand Dinars in Hasbi Ash-Shiddieqy’s Tafsir An-Nuur This study examines Muhammad Hasbi Ash-Shiddieqy’s interpretation of QS. At-Ṭalāq: 2–3, widely known as the “verse of one thousand dinars,” through a text-based exegetical analysis. The study focuses on Hasbi’s contextual-rational approach in interpreting the verse, especially the relationship between spiritual values such as taqwa and tawakkal and ethical responsibility within Qur’anic legal discourse. Using a qualitative method based on library research and content analysis, the study shows that Hasbi explains the normative-legal setting of divorce and waiting periods while developing an ethical framework in which divine provision (rizq) is linked to moral discipline and lawful conduct. The findings indicate that, in Hasbi’s interpretation, QS. At-Ṭalāq: 2–3 functions as a normative structure that integrates legal obedience, spiritual assurance, and ethical accountability. Sustenance is understood in material and moral terms, including ease of affairs, inner tranquility, and socially responsible behaviour grounded in taqwa. title: The Concept of Uswah Hasanah and Its Implementation in Islamic Family Education
text_snippet: The Concept of Uswah Hasanah and Its Implementation in Islamic Family Education This study examines uswah hasanah as a pedagogical model in Islamic family education and addresses a recurring gap in prior discussions that often emphasize exemplary conduct as a moral ideal without offering an operational framework that parents can apply in everyday family life. Using a descriptive qualitative approach through a literature review, this article synthesizes peer reviewed studies and scholarly sources published between 2016 and 2025 that discuss uswah hasanah, exemplary education, and Islamic family education. The analysis was conducted through close reading and thematic coding to identify recurring concepts, implementation mechanisms, and educational outcomes associated with exemplary education in the family context. The findings indicate that the family as madrasah al ula is a decisive setting for character formation because children internalize values primarily through repeated observation of parental conduct. The synthesis further shows that the implementation of uswah hasanah can be organized into five interrelated dimensions, namely tarbiyah bi al qudwah, tarbiyah bi al adat, tarbiyah bi al mau idzah, tarbiyah bi al mulaahadzah, and tarbiyah bi al uquubah, whi

title: The Feminization of Migration and Indonesia’s Protection Diplomacy for Female Migrant Workers in Malaysia Following the 2022 MoU
text_snippet: The Feminization of Migration and Indonesia’s Protection Diplomacy for Female Migrant Workers in Malaysia Following the 2022 MoU Indonesian female migrant workers continue to experience structural vulnerabilities, particularly in domestic and informal sectors where legal protection remains limited. These conditions are closely associated with the feminization of migration, which places women in undervalued care and domestic work shaped by gender inequality and uneven labor governance. In response to persistent protection challenges, Indonesia and Malaysia signed the 2022 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the Placement and Protection of Indonesian Domestic Migrant Workers, introducing institutional mechanisms such as the One Channel System (OCS). This study examines Indonesia’s protection diplomacy toward female migrant workers in Malaysia in the post-MoU period (2022–2025). Adopting a qualitative research design informed by a post-positivist perspective, the study employs document and content analysis of bilateral policy documents, official reports and statistics from the Indonesian Migrant Workers Protection Agency (BP2MI), and relevant academic literature on gendered migration and labor vulnerability. title: Down Payment Refund Clauses in Non-Cash Home Purchases (Taqsit): A Murabaḥah-Based Assessment of Gharar at PT Hadrah Aceh Pratama
text_snippet: Down Payment Refund Clauses in Non-Cash Home Purchases (Taqsit): A Murabaḥah-Based Assessment of Gharar at PT Hadrah Aceh Pratama This study examines the application of a murābaḥah framework in non-cash home purchases (taqsīṭ) at PT Hadrah Aceh Pratama, with particular attention to price disclosure and the down payment refund clause when a bank rejects a buyer’s financing application. Using a normative–empirical design, the analysis integrates doctrinal standards from fiqh al-muʿāmalah and DSN–MUI Fatwa No. 04/DSN-MUI/IV/2000 with field evidence drawn from written contracts, supporting transaction documents, observations, and interviews conducted on 25 October 2024 and 15 September 2025. The contracts set out the base cost, the agreed margin, and the installment schedule, while the down payment is determined by unit type. The central issue concerns the refund mechanism. The contract makes the refund contingent on the resale of the unit and does not stipulate a definite deadline. Although interviews indicate an internal target timeframe, the written clause leaves the time of performance open. This creates uncertainty (gharar) and falls short of the requirement of clarity (bayān) regarding obligations and timing in a valid murābaḥah arrangement. title: Utilization of Instagram as An Instrument of Public Policy Transparency: A Case Study of The Palangka Raya City Government
text_snippet: Utilization of Instagram as An Instrument of Public Policy Transparency: A Case Study of The Palangka Raya City Government The rapid development of digital communication has encouraged local governments to use social media to strengthen public policy transparency. Instagram, as a visually oriented and interactive platform, is increasingly adopted to disseminate policy information and public service messages. This study examines how the Palangka Raya City Government uses Instagram to support public policy transparency by focusing on: (1) the types of policy information communicated and their framing, (2) the dominant communication strategy pattern (push, pull, or networked), and (3) the implications of these practices for citizen interaction and perceived transparency. The study adopts a purposive case approach and qualitative content analysis. Data were drawn from peer-reviewed academic literature, official local government documents, publicly accessible Instagram content from relevant official accounts, and supporting news coverage (2019–2024). title: Mangroves in the North Rupat Landscape: Community Perceptions of Existence and Management
text_snippet: Mangroves in the North Rupat Landscape: Community Perceptions of Existence and Management Mangrove ecosystems play a critical role in coastal protection and the livelihoods of coastal communities, yet their sustainability is strongly influenced by how local people perceive mangrove existence and management. This study examines public perceptions of mangrove existence and management in Tanjung Medang and Teluk Rhu Villages, North Rupat District, and identifies factors shaping these perceptions. A quantitative descriptive approach was applied using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. From a population of 1,514 households, 48 respondents were selected using Slovin’s formula with a 10% margin of error and simple random sampling. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a one-sample t-test with a benchmark value of 108 (75% of the maximum ideal score). The results show that public perception of mangrove existence is positive across all components (total score 2,493), with the highest score in mangrove condition/state (1,212). title: Patterns of Cultural Adaptation in Marriage and Funeral Customs between Javanese and Acehnese Ethnic Groups in Sukadamai Village, Aceh Besar
text_snippet: Patterns of Cultural Adaptation in Marriage and Funeral Customs between Javanese and Acehnese Ethnic Groups in Sukadamai Village, Aceh Besar This study aims to analyze the cultural adaptation patterns of the Javanese community in their interaction with the Acehnese community in Gampong Sukadamai, Lembah Seulawah District, Aceh Besar Regency, particularly within the context of marriage and death rituals. This research employs a qualitative approach using observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation as data collection techniques. The findings reveal that cultural adaptation occurs gradually through social interaction, participation in communal and religious activities, and cooperation in economic practices. In the socio-cultural sphere, harmonious acculturation emerges, evidenced by the integration of Javanese and Acehnese elements in marriage rituals, communal feasts, and death ceremonies. The main challenges in adaptation involve differences in language, customs, and cultural values; however, these are overcome through effective communication, negotiation, and continuous interaction. title: Gender Inequality and Family Representation in The Film Andai Ibu Tidak Menikah Dengan Ayah
text_snippet: Gender Inequality and Family Representation in The Film Andai Ibu Tidak Menikah Dengan Ayah This study examines the representation of gender inequality in the Indonesian film Andai Ibu Tidak Menikah dengan Ayah and the circulation of its meanings through audience discourse on TikTok. Using a qualitative approach grounded in Fairclough’s Critical Discourse Analysis, the study analyzes the relationship between the filmic text, selected audience comments, and the broader social structures in which these discourses operate. The data consist of eight key scenes from the film and relevant TikTok responses that address domestic labor, emotional responsibility, and parental roles. The findings show that the film positions the mother as the narrative center who bears overlapping domestic, economic, and emotional burdens, while the father is represented through absent or destructive forms of masculinity. These representations contribute to the naturalization of women’s double burden within patriarchal family structures. At the same time, digital audience discourse reveals forms of discursive negotiation and critique, particularly from women who relate personal experiences to the film and question the moralization of maternal endurance. title: Muslim Community Perceptions of Sharia Boundaries in Interactions with Siblings-in-Law in Pahandut District
text_snippet: Muslim Community Perceptions of Sharia Boundaries in Interactions with Siblings-in-Law in Pahandut District Interaction with siblings-in-law occupies a sensitive position in Muslim family life, particularly in extended-family households where daily proximity is common. Although Islamic law clearly categorizes siblings-in-law as non-mahram, social practice often treats them as close family members, resulting in interaction patterns that blur sharia boundaries. This study examines how Muslim communities in Pahandut District understand and practice boundaries of interaction with siblings-in-law, and the factors that shape these practices. Using a qualitative field-based approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews with community members and a local religious figure, supported by document analysis. The findings show that community understanding of interaction boundaries varies significantly, influenced by kinship traditions, living arrangements, and uneven levels of religious literacy.
